blockNote: Four ramp-jump launcher actors (ramp_east, ramp_west, ramp_north, ramp_south; Bank 00, 53971-54829). Each one watches the player; when the player runs into its window the ramp takes the player's script over, locks the controls and carries the player a fixed distance along one axis. East/west ramps spawn a child actor that adds a precomputed vertical arc, so the player leaps; north/south ramps just move the player vertically for a number of animation cycles. Earlier notes called them collision tiles; they are actors placed through scene_actors.
=== PER-FRAME WATCH (two stages) ===
All four are actor-def <#00,#00,#20> and follow one pattern, mirrored per direction:

1. Stage 1 (every frame): RampCheckPlayerSpeed passes when |speed| on the ramp's axis (playerSpeedEw for east/west, playerSpeedNs for north/south) is at least 6 and playerFlags bit $0800 (script lock) is clear. Then the player must be inside the ramp's window (table below). When both hold the ramp executes SetEntryHere and enters stage 2.

2. Stage 2: every frame the ramp compares the player's position on the ramp's axis with its own. When the two are EXACTLY equal it fires the launch. If the distance grows to $10 or more it goes back to stage 1 with JumpNextFrame. Speed and lock are not rechecked in stage 2.
| Ramp | Axis | Window (player minus ramp) | Direction of the climb | Exit speed |
| ramp_east  | X, |dy| <= $18 | +2 .. +15 (player just east) | west (-8 per frame) | $FFF8 |
| ramp_west  | X, |dy| <= $18 | -16 .. -2 (player just west) | east (+8 per frame) | $0008 |
| ramp_north | Y, |dx| <= $10 | +2 .. +15 (player just south) | north (-8 per frame) | $FFF8 on playerSpeedNs |
| ramp_south | Y, |dx| <= $10 | -16 .. -2 (player just north) | south (+8 per frame) | $0008 on playerSpeedNs |

The direction of the speed is not tested: any |speed| >= 6 on the axis arms the ramp. The names describe the side the ramp sits on relative to the player. Chain $10 / $0F of movement_delta_table are the constant -8 / +8 per frame movements used by StagePlayerMoveXY. The ramp keeps its temporary window edge in the global words $0018 (east/west) and $001C (south) rather than in its own direct page; nothing yields between writing and using them.
=== LAUNCH (RampBeginPlayerControl) ===

The ramp writes the climb routine's address into the player's entry pointer ($00 / $02 of playerActor), then calls RampBeginPlayerControl: it zeroes playerSpeedEw and playerSpeedNs, stores the ramp's own $0E (the spawn-record type byte >> 1) into the player's statsPtr, zeroes the player's $2C / $2E, masks the D-pad ($0F00 into joypadMaskStd) and sets playerFlags $0800. The ramp itself then restarts at stage 1 and stays blocked by the $0800 lock until RestorePlayerControl clears it. The $0E value is the ramp's parameter: the arc selector for east/west and the loop count for north/south.
=== EAST / WEST CLIMB (RampPlayerClimbEast, loc_00D4F5) ===

Runs as the player. COP [SpawnAfter] func_00D5C0 creates the arc child right after the player (the child's $04 link is the player, the player's $06 link is the child); the player then writes the exit speed ($FFF8 east ramp, $0008 west ramp) into the child's orbitDiameter, clears $0008 in its own $10 (collision-aware movement off) and sets $0200, and loops StagePlayerMoveXY plus AnimOnce forever: animation $21 with X chain $10 (-8 per frame) for east, animation $24 with chain $0F (+8) for west. The loop ends because the child restores the player's entry.

func_00D5C0 reads the player's statsPtr (0 or 1), multiplies by 3 to index ramp_motion_curves (pointer + frame count), and from then on adds one sign-extended byte of the chosen curve to the player's Y ($16) each frame (ramp_motion_curve_step). After the last frame it copies orbitDiameter into playerSpeedEw, calls stair_climb.RestorePlayerControl, sets slopeStepCounter = 0 and decelStepCounter = 7 and dies.

Spawn type byte 1 ($0E = 0) selects ramp_curve_arc_64: 64 frames, rising up to 204 pixels (peak at frame 28) and returning to the start height (sum 0), about 512 pixels of horizontal travel. Spawn type 3 ($0E = 1) selects ramp_curve_arc_32: 32 frames, peak rise 50 pixels, ending 8 pixels lower (sum +8), about 256 pixels of travel. Only the Itory ramp pair (scene 15) uses type 1; every other east/west ramp uses type 3. These distances are static estimates (8 px x frames); they were not measured at runtime.
=== NORTH / SOUTH CLIMB (loc_00D518, RampPlayerClimbSouth) ===

No child and no arc. The player's loopCounter is set to statsPtr (the ramp's $0E: type $09 = 4, $0B = 5, $11 = 8, $03 = 1) and each loop iteration is StagePlayerMoveXY plus AnimOnce, i.e. one full animation cycle of Y movement at -8 (north, animation $1E, chain $10) or +8 (south, animation $19, chain $0F) per frame. After the loop playerSpeedNs = $FFF8 (north) or $0008 (south), RestorePlayerControl runs and the two step counters are reset as above. LoopEnd decrements before testing, so a count of 0 would run 65536 iterations; the placed ramps never use 0.
=== PLACEMENT ===

58 actor-spawn lines in scene_actors: 26 ramp_east, 22 ramp_west, 6 ramp_north, 4 ramp_south, in scenes 15, 1E, 21, 23, 4F, 53, 82, 83, 85 (Great Wall wall_rampway), 88, A1-A3, A5, A7 (A1, A2 and A5 are in mountain_temple/), B3, B5, CE, CF and D6 (pyramid/). East/west ramps use type 3 except the Itory pair; north uses type 9 (one type 3 in scene 21); south uses type $0B in scene 21 and $11 elsewhere.
=== QUIRKS ===

- Two label pairs are swapped relative to the direction: ramp_east_step is the loop head of the NORTH climb and ramp_north_step the loop head of the SOUTH climb; loc_00D518 is the north entry and loc_00D4F5 the west entry.
- The launch needs exact equality of the player and ramp coordinates on the axis in stage 2. Whether the player's step size always hits it was not checked at runtime.

- RampPlayerClimbEast stores the exit speed through LDX $06 without checking that SpawnAfter succeeded; if the actor pool were full the climb loop would never end. No evidence that this happens in practice.
- The player's $10 bit $0200 is set here and by stair_climb; its reader is unknown (see OQ-I032-5).

code_00D2D5: ramp_east stage 1 (re-entered by JumpNextFrame). Scratch $0018 = ramp X + 8, then the speed, row (|dy| <= $18) and column (player X - ramp X in 2..15) checks. RTL leaves the ramp at this entry for the next frame.
loc_00D316: ramp_east stage 2: SetEntryHere again, then compare player X with ramp X each frame. Equal: loc_00D334 launches. Distance >= $10: back to stage 1. Otherwise keep waiting.
loc_00D334: ramp_east launch: point the player's entry at RampPlayerClimbEast, run RampBeginPlayerControl, return to stage 1.
code_00D34D: ramp_west stage 1. Scratch $0018 = ramp X - 8; the window is player X - ramp X in -16..-2.
loc_00D3A6: ramp_west launch: the player's entry becomes loc_00D4F5 (the west climb).
code_00D3BF: ramp_north stage 1: axis Y. Checks playerSpeedNs, |player X - ramp X| <= $10 and player Y - ramp Y in 2..15.
loc_00D3F6: ramp_north stage 2: compare player Y with ramp Y each frame.
loc_00D414: ramp_north launch: the player's entry becomes loc_00D518 (the north climb).
code_00D42D: ramp_south stage 1: scratch $001C = ramp Y - $10; the window is player Y - ramp Y in -16..-2 with |dx| <= $10.
loc_00D464: ramp_south stage 2: compare player Y with ramp Y each frame.
loc_00D482: ramp_south launch: the player's entry becomes RampPlayerClimbSouth.
RampBeginPlayerControl: Takes the player over: zero both speeds, statsPtr = ramp $0E (curve index or loop count), zero player $2C / $2E, mask the D-pad ($0F00) and set playerFlags $0800. Y = player actor on entry; X = the ramp.
RampCheckPlayerSpeed: A = signed speed on the ramp's axis. Carry clear = |speed| >= 6 and playerFlags $0800 clear; carry set otherwise.
RampPlayerClimbEast: East-ramp climb (runs as the player): spawn the arc child, give it the exit speed $FFF8, then loop animation $21 with X chain $10 (-8 per frame) until the child restores control.
loc_00D4F5: West-ramp climb (unnamed in the original): same as RampPlayerClimbEast with exit speed $0008, animation $24 and X chain $0F (+8 per frame).
loc_00D518: North-ramp climb entry: loopCounter = statsPtr, loop head ramp_east_step. Clears $0008 / sets $0200 in the player's $10.
ramp_east_step: Loop head of the NORTH climb (the name is swapped): animation $1E, Y chain $10 (-8 per frame), one animation cycle per iteration; after the last iteration playerSpeedNs = $FFF8 and control is restored.
RampPlayerClimbSouth: South-ramp climb entry: loopCounter = statsPtr, loop head ramp_north_step, SetEntryHere, clears $0008 / sets $0200 in the player's $10.
ramp_north_step: Loop head of the SOUTH climb (the name is swapped): animation $19, Y chain $0F (+8 per frame), one animation cycle per iteration; after the last iteration playerSpeedNs = $0008 and control is restored.
func_00D5C0: Arc driver child of the east/west climbs. X = $04 link = the player. Selects the curve from the player's statsPtr, sets loopCounter = frame count and orbitAngle = byte offset of the curve, then runs ramp_motion_curve_step once per frame. At the end: playerSpeedEw = orbitDiameter (exit speed), RestorePlayerControl, step counters reset, COP Die.
ramp_motion_curve_step: One frame of the arc: read the next signed byte of the curve (orbitAngle + frame index $2A), sign-extend and add it to the player's Y at $16. LoopEnd repeats it once per frame for the curve's frame count.

ramp_motion_curves: Two arc entries (3 bytes each: curve address, frame count) used by func_00D5C0 in ramps.asm. The ramp's arc child reads the player's statsPtr (0 or 1, set from the ramp's spawn type byte) x 3, then adds one sign-extended curve byte per frame to the PLAYER's Y ($16, confirmed: the child's $04 link is the spawner, the player). Values are pixel deltas. Entry 0: 64 frames, rises up to 204 pixels (frame 28) and returns, net 0. Entry 1: 32 frames, rises up to 50 pixels (frame 14), net +8 (ends 8 pixels lower). Both curves repeat most values twice in a row.
ramp_curve_arc_64: Entry 0 of ramp_motion_curves: 64 signed Y deltas in pixels, one per frame, -16 at the start, 0 around frames 29-36 and +16 at the end. Cumulative rise peaks at -204 (up) at frame 28; the sum is 0. Used by the Itory ramp pair (spawn type 1).
ramp_curve_arc_32: Entry 1 of ramp_motion_curves: 32 signed Y deltas in pixels, -8 at the start, 0 at frames 15-17 and +8 at the end. Cumulative rise peaks at -50 (up) at frame 14; the sum is +8, so the player lands 8 pixels lower. Used by all other east/west ramps (spawn type 3).

blockNote: Spawn-time-gated palette swap for the South Cape area after the Kara-news cutscene (Bank 00, 46530-46558). Spawned in scene 01 (South Cape) and scene 30 (Oakton).
=== GATE ===

Two BranchOnFlagByte checks run once when the thinker spawns: kill itself if event flag $1C is set, kill itself if event flag $16 is clear. Flag $16 is set by sc02_erik (the coastal-cave Kara-news cutscene) and $1C by sc06_monologue (Will's end-of-day narration), so the thinker lives in the window between those two events. The loop target is after the gate, so the flags are not checked again.
=== BODY ===
PaletteStart #02 plus PaletteStep applies palette bundle $02: a single 1-frame step that writes 80 colours starting at colour index $30 (decoded from the bundle table, delay 0).

The thinker then sets event flag $FF itself and WaitOnFlagByte ( #FF, #00 ) parks until $FF is clear. $FF is the scene-setup-complete latch: scene_lifecycle clears it at the top of scene setup and again sets it at the end, and the inventory overlay clears it on open; both set it again when their setup finishes. The thinker list is rebuilt on every scene change, so within one scene visit the loop normally plays the bundle once; whether it resumes after an inventory open/close was not checked (the loop would replay the bundle).
The spawn-record parameter byte is ignored (the bundle id is an immediate). Setting $FF early is a side effect on a shared flag; no other flag-$FF watcher was found in the lists of these scenes.
In Oakton (scene 30) flag $1C is expected to be set already (it is never cleared in extracted/), so there the gate kills the thinker at once - inferred, not run.
The earlier notes ('kills itself when conditions flip', 'many interior and Dark Space scenes') were wrong: the gate is evaluated only at spawn and only the scenes listed above spawn this thinker.

FlagGatedPaletteWarmKill: Target of the gate: KillThinker, then RTL. Reached only at spawn.
loc_00B5CE: Palette loop: apply bundle $02 once, set flag $FF, wait until $FF is clear, then repeat (the gate above is not re-evaluated).
